title: docs: README, readme.txt and screenshots for SEO Pro Custom's purpose
body:
## What and why

The README and `readme.txt` now cover only what SEO Pro Custom is for: changing how a site's theme or plugins behave when their settings can't, without waiting on their makers, and how to do it.

- **README.md**: new intro; When to use it (setting → documented hook → CSS → code); Make your own copy; Make a change (worked example with a real string and a domain-specific `gettext_{domain}` filter, header table); Check your changes (the four states, Settings, Site Health, `wp seoprocustom list`); Ask for a change upstream; Keep your copy up to date; Release your copy. Then the shared parts: Report a problem, Requirements, Uninstall, a short Developers pointer, Changelog, Built with AI, Works well with SEO Pro Stack, License and the managed block.
- Dropped the starter's settings screen, multisite network settings and long filter list (SEO Pro Custom has no settings of its own); Developers links to the starter for those.
- Fixed the banner alt text ("Customise your site safely") and the duplicated starter copyright line.
- **readme.txt**: same purpose; no longer names SEO Pro Stack (preflight's Recommendation rule); new FAQ entries (when to use it, what happens when upstream catches up); screenshot captions match the new screenshots.
- **seoprocustom.php** `Description:` matches the new short description (145 characters).
- **Screenshots**: `screenshot-1.png` (Customisations card: loaded, skipped, retired, failed), `screenshot-2.png` (Site Health item for a failed file), `docs/images/github-update.png` (SEO Pro Custom offered an update), and the `.webp` copies.
- **DCO for outside contributions only**: `.github/workflows/dco.yml` skips the job for pull requests from a branch of this repository (outside contributions come from forks). Without this, every maintainer and background-worker PR fails it (#6 merged with it failing), and so would a client's own PRs in their private copy. A first try keyed on `author_association` still ran the job for an organisation member's PR, so it was replaced. Checked with `actionlint`.
- **Badges**: `scripts/readme-badges.sh --codacy … --add codefactor` put the Codacy and CodeFactor badges in the starter's order (both badge images return 200).

Replaces #7 (same commits, now signed off).

## How it was tested

- `scripts/test-site.sh up --ref HEAD` (WordPress 7.1.4, PHP 8.3) with four demo customisation files written on the test site only. `wp seoprocustom list` showed the expected states: footer-phone loaded; listing-call-label skipped (`Requirement not met: …`, the plugin it needs is not installed); hide-post-dates retired; related-services failed (`Call to undefined function … (line 7)`); example skipped.
- Screenshots taken with Playwright from that site and checked by eye.
- `scripts/build-banner.sh`: banner and icon outputs rebuilt byte-identical; screenshot copies updated.

Follows #5 (banner and icon) and #2 (the build). Ref #2

<!-- aidevops:origin:interactive -->

title: chore(release): 0.1.1 with the Customisations card split into its own class
body:
## Summary

This PR releases 0.1.1, which includes #13 (strapline and fork README), #12 (part of #10) and #14 (#8, card padding). It also fixes two problems #14 introduced:

- **SonarCloud quality gate:** #14 failed it with php:S1448, because `SEOProCustom_Customizations` reached 21 methods. The Customisations card and its inline style now live in a new class, `SEOProCustom_Customizations_Admin` (`includes/features/class-seoprocustom-customizations-admin.php`). It is loaded in wp-admin only, the same way the CLI class is loaded only under WP-CLI. The loader class is back to 18 methods.
- **Preflight "Core class names" warning:** #14 hid the starter's "No settings yet" placeholder through the internal `.spc-empty` class. It is now hidden with `.spc-section > .spc-card:has(+ .spc-customisations)`, which uses public core classes only. With settings present, the tab renders an `.spc-cards` list instead, so the selector doesn't match.
- The card's intro now says "in your fork of this plugin", to match the README.
- **Release 0.1.1:** the version is set in `seoprocustom.php` (header and constant), `readme.txt` and `README.md`. There are changelog entries in all three places, and the badges were regenerated with `scripts/readme-badges.sh`.
- **Screenshots:** both were retaken at 0.1.1 and the `.webp` copies rebuilt. The demo's "requirement not met" example now uses `woocommerce >= 9.0`.

## Verification

- `scripts/lint.sh`: everything passed (php, js, shell, workflows, phpcs, phpstan).
- `scripts/preflight-release.sh --no-docker`: 0 errors. The two remaining warnings are known: the WordPress.org slug note, and three core files that wait on the starter's own blocks (#10, starter #686).
- Docker test site (WordPress 7.1.4, PHP 8.3), with five demo customisation files:
  - Settings → SEO Pro Custom shows the card with inner padding and the placeholder hidden.
